articles.title: Victor Glover, First Black Astronaut to Fly to the Moon, Signs With CAA (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: CAA has signed astronaut Victor Glover for representation in all areas. Glover is a retired U.S. Navy captain and an emeritus NASA astronaut, making history several times throughout his career as a space explorer.
body: Before Glover was selected to be an astronaut in 2013, during a term as a legislative fellow in the U.S. Senate, he’d built a successful career as a Naval aviator. Glover was a test pilot in the F/A‐18 Hornet, Super Hornet and EA‐18G Growler and has flown over 45 aircraft, accumulating over 4000 hours in the skies. He has been awarded the Defense Superior Service Medal, Navy Commendation Medal, two Navy and Marine Corps Achievement Medals, NASA Distinguished Service Medal and NASA Space Exploration Medal.

The California native is a alum of California Polytechnic State University, where he now serves as an executive advisor. He also hold Masters degrees from the Naval Postgraduate School and has been awarded honorary Doctorates from California Polytechnic State University and Howard University.
points: CAA has signed astronaut Victor Glover for representation in all areas.

articles.title: Kristen Stewart, Riley Keough and Wagner Moura to Star in Olivier Assayas’ Next Film ‘Spiritual World’
articles.summary: French director Olivier Assayas (“The Wizard of the Kremlin”) has set his next movie, “Spiritual World,” with a starry cast including Kristen Stewart, Vicky Krieps, Riley Keough and Wagner Moura.
body: The film will start shooting in February in France and Germany with an international cast that also includes Barbara Sukowa (“Deux”) and Niels Schneider (“The Unknown”).

Assayas is also reteaming with Paris-based producer Olivier Delbosc for “Spirtual World.” The pair worked together on Assayas’ latest film “The Wizard of the Kremlin,” an ambitious political thriller with Jude Law portraying Russian President Vladimir Putin and Paul Dano a spin doctor named Vadim Baranov. The movie, which also starred Alicia Vikander, world premiered at the Venice Film Festival.
Arte France, the Franco-German network, is co-financing the film which is currently being developed by Delbosc without a French studio attached.

One of Europe’s most celebrated auteurs, Assayas has been navigating between French and international projects spanning different genres for decades. He notably directed Cuban Five (“WASP Network”), an espionage thriller starring Edgar Ramírez, Penélope Cruz and Gael García Bernal; and the HBO mini-series “Irma Vep” with Vikander.

articles.title: Matt Groening on the Future of ‘Futurama’ as the Series Gets Another Finale: ‘We Will Rise Again’ (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: “Futurama” is over. Long live “Futurama!” As the long-running animated series wraps its Season 14 Monday on Hulu, there are no further plans at the moment for it to return as a regular series. (However, three supersized Hulu specials are still to come).
body: “Futurama” first premiered on Fox in 1999 but ended its run there in 2003. Comedy Central revived it in 2008 and wrapped the show up in 2013. It returned again in 2023 via Hulu.

Each time the show went away, or it looked like the series was ending, the producers prepared an episode that could double as a series finale — only for the show to later come back. That’s why the producers had some fun with the episodic name for the year’s latest “finale.” Monday’s episode — the “Futurama” Season 14 ender — was given the title “Final Ending: The Last Conclusion.” The episode is a bit of an origins/flashback story; here’s the logline: “Fry and his brother sneak into a PG-13 movie as kids … with shocking consequences for the future.”
And yes, this could always double as a regular series finale. But don’t bet on it.

articles.title: Pandora’s Legacy review – fascinating profile of silent film legend GW Pabst
articles.summary: Through intimate letters and family interviews, this probing documentary about the Austrian film-maker reveals a complicated figure. A titan of silent cinema, Austrian director GW Pabst left behind a treasure trove of classics.
body: Far from a hagiographic portrait, Christlieb’s film reveals Pabst to be a complicated and patriarchal figure. His grandchildren – Marion, Daniel and Ben – describe the great film-maker as a distant figure, who instilled fear rather than love in his two sons. Pabst’s films have been praised for their modern and strong-willed female characters, yet in private he forbade Gertrude from pursuing her own acting aspirations. She also reluctantly underwent numerous abortions – seven in total – so as not to derail her husband’s career.
points: Through intimate letters and family interviews, this probing documentary about the Austrian film-maker reveals a complicated figure.

articles.title: Crushed review – Steve Oram is priestly lead in harrowing Bangkok-set child-abduction thriller
articles.summary: A priest investigates his daughter’s kidnapping in Thailand in this Paul Schrader-esque inquiry into spiritual nihilism. ‘He’s American, a little bit overweight, sweaty, a little bit camp, creepy.” As far as descriptions of border-hopping paedophiles go, this seems a little on the nose.
body: Pastor to a mixed Anglo-Thai congregation, Father Daniel has a young daughter, Olivia (Margaux Dietrich), with wife May (Nattapohn Rawddon). At a sleepover, Olivia is traumatised when her friend’s older brother shows her a “crush” video of a kitten being stomped by a scantily clad floozy. So when her own cat Missy goes awol, she is convinced the same lady is responsible, and asks her dad how God could let it happen. The family mobilise to track down Missy, but Olivia in turn disappears one day after school, kicking off Father Daniel’s own test of faith.

There could have been a very different version of Crushed, if Liam Neeson had signed on with his special set of ecumenical skills. But Rumley holds the vengeance angle at bay, subtly foreshadowing Olivia’s ordeal with the implied horror of the squashed furballs filtering through her nightmares, and using clever juxtaposition to slyly compare and contrast her father’s lofty ideals with the surrounding scrappy reality. At one point, after refusing to play the Beatles’ profane songs, Father Daniel’s acoustic guitar version of All Creatures Great and Small soundtracks Olivia’s pet search on the streets.

articles.title: ‘Should have garnered the actor an Oscar’: why Liar Liar is my feelgood movie
articles.summary: The latest in our series of writers paying tribute to the films they watch when they need a lift is an appreciation of Jim Carrey’s manic 90s comedy. To be completely honest, whenever anybody asks what my favorite movies are, my list has some typical standbys: Goodfellas and It’s a Wonderful Life…
body: The movie (for the lack of a better word) lies on the bedrock of a simple premise: a lawyer and doting father is physically unable to tell an untruth due to a birthday wish. In the hands of a less competent creative team and cast, Liar Liar would have been yet another forgettable piece of 90s comedy junk; destined for the bottom of a discount VHS bin, forgotten as the years trudged on. But largely thanks to an unbelievable performance courtesy of Carrey, who was working with a smart and peppy script, the film ascends into rarefied air.

The bellylaugh-o-meter breaks its springs on a regular basis throughout its brisk 86-minute runtime. In fact, it’s on par, or even surpassing, fellow comedy powerhouses such as Airplane! and The Naked Gun when it comes to the sheer volume of gags, set pieces and jokes. Tom Shadyac, the director, who previously directed Carrey in his 1993 breakout Ace Ventura: Pet Detective, wisely unleashes Carrey, who spins out and around the scenery like the Tasmanian Devil, remarkably combining such a manic and energetic performance with one grounded in pure emotion.
points: The latest in our series of writers paying tribute to the films they watch when they need a lift is an appreciation of Jim Carrey’s manic 90s comedy.

articles.title: Slipknot fans hit back after Marilyn Manson announced as support act for UK show
articles.summary: The heavy metal band will be joined by the US rock musician during their London show.
body: Heavy metal band Slipknot have announced a new world tour, with Marilyn Manson due to appear as a support act.
The eight-piece group, known for performing in masks, will be joined by the US rock musician during their shows at London's Wembley Stadium and multiple dates of the South American leg of the tour.
Some fans have reacted angrily to the news and said they will not attend the shows over past sexual abuse accusations against the 57-year-old.
Manson, real name Brian Warner, has always strongly denied any allegations against him.

articles.title: Just Play Dead review – Samuel L Jackson and Eva Green punch up switchback crime caper
articles.summary: Jackson and Green just about manage to distract viewers from the sub-par Tarantinoesque flourishes, confusing plot points and tired stereotypes. Having shot five films since 2020, 82-year-old Martin Campbell is a certified member of the post-retirement director’s club that includes Ridley Scott…
body: Interrupting his retirement on a Spanish-speaking Caribbean island with the odd poisoning (seen in the intro), kingpin Jack Wolfe (Jackson) is getting antsy. Afraid the law is close behind him, he hatches a scheme with his philandering wife Nora (Eva Green): help him frame her surfer lover Chad (Jason Fernández) for his supposed murder, and they will split the big-bucks insurance payout. He covers his back for the possibility she might do him in for real by recording her saying as much. But she ropes Chad anyway into her murder conspiracy, plotting to let him take the fall – or perhaps her detective bit on the side Dani (Eoin Macken) will get there first.

articles.title: ‘Heil Jupiter!’ Review: Mexican Arthouse Auteur Carlos Reygadas Takes a Beguiling Cinematic Trip to Nowhere
articles.summary: The latest feature from the director of 'Silent Light' and 'Post Tenebras Lux' was shot across several continents in different languages, including one invented for the film.
body: Iconoclastic Mexican director Carlos Reygadas continues to test the boundaries of cinema, and the patience of many a viewer, in his latest audaciously executed head trip, Heil Jupiter!

The Mexican auteur started off in the early aughts with a trio of strikingly directed arthouse flicks ( Japón, Battle in Heaven, Silent Light ) combining a form of minimalist realism with something more animalistic and otherworldly, as if the work of Robert Bresson had been rejiggered by Terence Malick. For his fourth feature, Post Tenebras Lux, Reygadas took a major detour toward the avant-garde and the personal, in a move that garnered him some detractors while pleasing his more hardcore fans. He went even further with 2018’s Nuestro tiempo, which felt much more self-indulgent than exploratory.

articles.title: ‘Street Fighter’ Filmmaker Kitao Sakurai, Netflix’s Jinny Howe and Women of ‘The Pitt’ Set as Honorees for Milestone CAPE Gala
articles.summary: Presented by Lexus, the Oct. 3 gala will also honor actor Ben Wang and Walt Disney Animation Studios' Kalikolehua Hurley and feature presenters Auliʻi Cravalho, Nisha Ganatra, Ali Ahn, Sherry Cola, Lilly Singh and Callina Liang.
body: CAPE, the Coalition of Asian Pacifics in Entertainment, has added more boldfaced names to the program for its milestone 35th anniversary gala.

Leading those new trophies, Sakurai is set to receive a Visionary Award ahead of the Oct. 16 release from Paramount of his video game adaptation starring Noah Centineo, Andrew Koji, Callina Liang, Jason Momoa and David Dastmalchian. Known for his long-running work with pal Eric Andre on his The Eric Andre Show, Sakurai has also directed and executive produced projects like Beef, Dave, Twisted Metal, Bad Trip and Butterfly.

Wang will be feted with CAPE’s Rising Star Award ahead of Lionsgate’s Nov. 20 bow of the latest Hunger Games film from Francis Lawrence. His previous credits include Disney+’s American Born Chinese, Karate Kid: Legends and the dystopian thriller The Long Walk, also helmed by Lawrence.
